summary: Computes motion vectors from an input image, outputting horizontal motion in red and vertical motion in green as 32-bit floating point screen-width-per-second values.

key_params.name: gridsize
key_params.note: Output grid: grid1x1, grid2x2, or grid4x4.

key_params.name: quality
key_params.note: High, medium, or low optical-flow quality/speed tradeoff.

key_params.name: costoutput
key_params.note: Output uncertainty/cost in the blue channel.

key_params.name: gain
key_params.note: Post-scale R/X and G/Y flow values.

key_params.name: manualtiming
key_params.note: Use explicit timestamps for sources whose frame rate differs from the project.

key_params.name: timestamp
key_params.note: Video-frame timestamp in seconds when manual timing is enabled.

common_gotchas: Official docs mark Optical Flow TOP as Windows-only.
Requires an NVIDIA 3000-series or higher GPU.
Turing GPUs only support 4x4 grid size; newer GPUs can use all grid options.
Higher quality and smaller grids produce larger/slower outputs.
Manual Timing needs a reliable per-frame timestamp, often from an Info CHOP on the video source.
key_concepts: Detects motion patterns in an input image.
Outputs horizontal motion in red and vertical motion in green.
Motion values are 32-bit float screen-width-per-second data, not display colors.
Optional cost output writes uncertainty/cost into the blue channel.
